title: Native interop use cases
description: What an application developer does to move values between Rust's own time types and UTV.

entities.name: Bring a native date/time value in and out
entities.description: A developer turns a clock reading or a chrono value into a UTV value with the intent named, works with it, and turns it back into a native value when the native type can hold it. The shared code intent-required has no branch here: the intent is the target type, so a call without one doesn't compile.
entities.goal: Use a value from SystemTime or chrono with UTV, and get a native value back, without UTV guessing what it meant or reading the host.
preconditions: The developer's crate depends on utv; for chrono's types, with the cargo feature chrono.
The developer holds the native value: a reading they took themselves (SystemTime::now(), Utc::now()) or a chrono value.
postconditions: The UTV value holds exactly what the native value held, as the kind the developer named, or the developer has Diagnostics saying why it could not be taken.
Converted back, the native value is the one UTV held, or an error names what would have been lost.

flow.action: Reads the clock, or takes a chrono value, in their own code; the library never does this for them.

Converts it with the type that names the intent: Instant::from_system_time(reading), CivilDate::from(naive_date), CivilDateTime::try_from(naive_date_time), Instant::try_from(date_time) or FixedOffsetDateTime::try_from(date_time).
Writes the native fields as UTV JSON (from_system_time, from_naive_date_time, from_fixed_offset, from_utc) and reads the typed value from it with the typed layer's checks.

Converts a UTV value back: NaiveDate::try_from(date), NaiveDateTime::try_from(date_time), DateTime::<FixedOffset>::try_from(fixed), DateTime::<Utc>::try_from(instant) or SystemTime::try_from(instant).
Builds the native value from the UTV value, exactly, or returns Err(Diagnostics) with the loss it would have caused.

alternatives.condition: The value is a chrono DateTime<Local>, tied to the host's zone.
alternatives.outcome: No typed conversion exists; the JSON-layer from_local answers unsupported (local-zone), pointing to from_fixed_offset or from_utc.

alternatives.condition: chrono holds a leap second (a nanosecond field of 10^9 or more).
alternatives.outcome: Err with leap-second: UTV would need a leap-second table.

alternatives.condition: A DateTime<FixedOffset> has an offset beyond ±18:00 and the target is FixedOffsetDateTime.
The year is outside chrono's range (about ±262 000), or the instant outside SystemTime's or chrono's.
The instant has a fraction finer than a nanosecond, or finer than this platform's SystemTime.
Through the JSON-layer functions, a zoned or fixed-offset value goes to a naive type, or a named-zone value to DateTime<FixedOffset>.
alternatives.outcome: Err with zone-dropped (unsupported): the native type would keep less than the value says.

relatedViews.relationship: The capability this use case uses.
